title: Wall Street Lines Up Behind Alphabet Ahead of Tuesday Earnings as AI Bets Intensify
excerpt: Bank of America, Wedbush, and Warren Buffett are all bullish on Google's parent company before its July 22 earnings report, with analysts pointing to cloud growth and a surging Anthropic stake.
body:
• Bank of America and Wedbush have reiterated buy ratings on Alphabet, citing strong Google Cloud growth and AI monetization potential ahead of July 22 earnings.
  • Warren Buffett has publicly confirmed initiating Berkshire Hathaway's Alphabet position, calling the stock "more likely to be a winner."
  • Analysts expect Q2 earnings per share near $5.11-$5.20, building on Q1 results that beat consensus by over 90 percent.
  • The stock trades at $346, down from a 52-week high of $408, as concerns about Gemini 3.5 Pro delays weigh on AI sentiment.

The Bull Case Builds

With Alphabet's Q2 earnings report set for Tuesday, July 22, Wall Street's biggest names are doubling down on the search and cloud giant. Bank of America has reiterated its buy rating, highlighting strong Google Cloud growth and a potentially undervalued stake in Anthropic, the AI startup behind Claude. Wedbush has set a $445 price target, implying nearly 30 percent upside from current levels.

The endorsements extend beyond traditional sell-side research. Warren Buffett publicly confirmed that he personally initiated Berkshire Hathaway's Alphabet investment, calling GOOG "more likely to be a winner" — a high-profile vote of confidence from the world's most famous value investor. Recent institutional filings show major players including Vanguard, State Street, and Norges Bank adding to their positions.

The Numbers to Watch

Alphabet's Q1 results set a high bar. The company reported $5.11 earnings per share, crushing the $2.68 consensus by more than 90 percent on revenue of $109.9 billion. Revenue grew 21.8 percent year-over-year, driven by strength across Google Search, YouTube, and Google Cloud.

For Q2, analysts project earnings per share in the $5.11-$5.20 range. Google Cloud's growth trajectory is the key variable — the segment has been accelerating as enterprises shift AI workloads to cloud infrastructure. Search revenue is also being closely watched for signs that AI-powered features are enhancing rather than cannibalizing traditional ad revenue.

The stock closed Friday at $346.12, down 2.2 percent on the session. Alphabet's market capitalization stands at roughly $4.2 trillion, with a price-to-earnings ratio of 26.4 and a PEG ratio of 1.48.

The Bear Case

Not everything is favorable. Reports of delays to Gemini 3.5 Pro have intensified concerns that Google is falling behind rivals OpenAI and Anthropic in the AI model race. The European Union has ordered Google to open Android and search data to rival AI companies, a regulatory move that could weaken its competitive moat. Recent insider selling has been heavy, with no insider purchases in the past six months.

A new securities-fraud investigation and reports that AI search tools may pose safety risks for children add headline risk heading into earnings.

What It Means for Investors

Alphabet remains one of the most widely held stocks among Indian-American investors, both directly and through index funds. The company employs thousands of Indian-origin engineers across its AI, cloud, and search divisions — CEO Sundar Pichai among them. Google Cloud's expansion has also made it a major employer in India, where it operates multiple data center regions.

For portfolio watchers, the consensus is clear: 5 strong-buy ratings, 27 buys, and just 4 holds, with an average price target of $383. Whether Alphabet can deliver on those expectations Tuesday will set the tone for Big Tech earnings season.
